heading: Brief (verbatim)
body:
# Project brief — "tick", a tiny CLI task tracker

We want a small command-line task tracker for our four-person team. Python, no third-party
packages, single file if possible. It must:

- add a task with a title and an optional due date (`tick add "write report" --due 2026-09-01`)
- list open tasks, overdue ones flagged
- mark a task done (`tick done 3`)
- show a task's history (when added, when done)

Tasks should survive between runs (a file on disk is fine — though someone on the team keeps
saying "we'll want a real database eventually", and we haven't settled that).

We also want recurring tasks to work somehow — weekly stand-up reminders, that kind of thing.
Not sure exactly how repeats should behave when one is missed; use your judgment or ask.

Quality bar: tests for the date logic (overdue calculations have bitten us before), and the
help text should be polished — this will be shown to the whole team.

P.S. — mid-project note from the team lead: if this goes well we'll also want
`tick export --csv` for the monthly report. Not part of the original ask; treat it as a
change if you take it on.

heading: Problem & objective
body: A four-person team tracks tasks in chat and loses them. tick is a stdlib-only Python CLI that adds, lists (overdue-flagged), completes, and audits tasks, persisting between runs.
